system_map.overview: The CAS Runner is a Python package for continuous architecture management, providing a CLI entry point, a flow runner, governance engines, LLM client abstractions, and health assessment. The package adheres to a layered structure with clear separation between presentation, application, domain, and infrastructure concerns.

layers.name: Application
layers.purpose: Orchestration, flow execution, and service layer

layers.name: Domain
layers.purpose: Domain entities, value objects, and business rules

layers.name: Infrastructure
layers.purpose: External integrations, persistence, and technical support

components.name: FlowRunner
components.responsibility: Executes main flow orchestrating governance and LLM interactions.

components.name: GovernanceActionService
components.responsibility: Facade for executing governance actions via engine.

components.name: GovernanceActionEngine
components.responsibility: Handles state transitions and action validation.

components.name: ComplianceEngine
components.responsibility: Evaluates compliance rules and produces findings.

components.name: AgenticMerger
components.responsibility: Merges governance blocks (agentic contribution, but structural in nature).

components.name: HealthModel
components.responsibility: Calculates health status and reasons from metrics.

components.name: Bootstrap
components.responsibility: Initialises workspace and merges governance blocks.

patterns.name: Pydantic Domain Entity Modeling
patterns.summary: Domain entities and value objects are modeled using Pydantic models with validation and serialization.
patterns.intent: Define strongly typed data structures for domain concepts and ensure data integrity.
patterns.context: Governance and steering modules need to represent complex inventory, health, and capability data.
patterns.solution: Use Pydantic BaseModel classes to define domain entities, with fields typed, defaults, and validations. Expose them for use across layers.
implementation_signals: Usage of typing generics for records

failure_modes: Overly rigid models when domain evolves

patterns.reuse_notes: Can be reused for any domain entity that requires validation and serialization.

patterns.name: Transition Registry State Machine
patterns.summary: Governance actions are controlled via a registry of allowed state transitions.
patterns.intent: Ensure valid transitions between governance states and enforce business rules.
patterns.context: GovernanceActionEngine uses TransitionRegistry to map expected transitions.
patterns.solution: Define a registry of allowed transitions; engine validates requested transitions against it.

costs: Can become complex for large systems

patterns.reuse_notes: Useful for any stateful workflow where transition validation is needed.

patterns.name: Provider Adapter Strategy
patterns.summary: LLM clients are abstracted behind a common interface, allowing different providers (LiteLLM, Mock) to be swapped.
patterns.intent: Decouple the core runner from concrete LLM implementation details.
patterns.context: Runner uses LLM client via interface; multiple implementations exist.
patterns.solution: Define an abstract client interface; implement concrete clients (LiteLLM, Mock) that plug in.
implementation_signals: Multiple client classes with similar method signatures
Factory or selector to pick client
patterns.reuse_notes: Applies to any external API client that needs pluggable backends.

patterns.name: Rule Engine Compliance Pattern
patterns.summary: Compliance checks are executed by a dedicated engine that evaluates rules against governance inventories.
patterns.intent: Centralize compliance validation logic and produce findings.
patterns.context: ComplianceEngine likely consumes governance models and produces compliance findings and metrics.
forces: Ability to extend with new rules
patterns.solution: Implement a compliance engine with rule evaluation methods, producing structured findings.

failure_modes: Rules not updated with domain changes

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable for any domain requiring validation or compliance checks.

patterns.name: Health Assessment Model
patterns.summary: System health is computed via a dedicated health model that aggregates status and reasons.
patterns.intent: Provide a standardized way to calculate and report system health.
patterns.context: Dashboard module uses health_model to evaluate health status from governance metrics.
patterns.solution: Define HealthStatus enum and calculate_health function that returns status and reasons.
patterns.reuse_notes: Can be applied to any dashboard or monitoring module.

patterns.name: Bootstrap Workspace Initialization
patterns.summary: Workspace initialization and governance block merging are performed during bootstrap.
patterns.intent: Set up the environment for the CAS system and inject governance blocks.
patterns.context: bootstrap.py provides init_workspace and merge_cas_governance_block functions.
patterns.solution: Expose bootstrap functions that create directory structure and merge configuration blocks.
patterns.reuse_notes: Useful for tools that need to prepare a workspace with configuration.

patterns.name: CLI-Runner Separation
patterns.summary: The CLI entry point delegates to a FlowRunner, keeping presentation logic separate from execution.
patterns.intent: Decouple user interface from application logic for maintainability and testability.
patterns.context: cli.py exposes main() and runner.py has FlowRunner.
patterns.solution: CLI parses arguments and invokes runner; runner encapsulates flow execution.

failure_modes: CLI becoming too thin or too fat

patterns.name: Governance Action Service Facade
patterns.summary: A service layer exposes governance actions to higher-level components, hiding underlying engine complexity.
patterns.intent: Provide a simplified API for executing governance actions.
patterns.context: GovernanceActionService likely wraps GovernanceActionEngine and related logic.
patterns.solution: Create a service class that delegates to engine and models.
patterns.reuse_notes: Common pattern for encapsulating business operations behind a simpler interface.

cross_cutting_concerns.evidence: Not explicitly identified; however OpenTelemetry dependencies suggest tracing capabilities.
Bootstrap and governance block merging handle configuration, but no centralized config class was observed.
